newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called flat to lower, cash softer.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called flat to lower, cash softer.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open flat to lower Tuesday after a steady ACCESS session and early talk of softer cash prices, market sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.20 to $2.215 after settling to the downside Monday at $2.215 per million British thermal units.
In ACCESS, June last traded unchanged at $2.215.
Meanwhile, cash prices at Henry Hub were talked a few cents lower at $2.18-2.22 per mmBtu amid moderate weather throughout most of the U.S.
Forecasts are calling for a continuation of normal to below-normal temperatures this week in the Northeast, Midwest and Texas. In the Southwest, seasonable weather is expected.
Technical traders pegged June support at $2.15 and then at $2.05. Resistance was seen at $2.30 and the $2.43 contract high.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd Tuesday through Thursday.

In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed about five cents to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to about $2.02-2.04. New York city gate gas was quoted more than five cents higher around $2.50.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report were about 55 bcf.
